editorial.marketOverview: Friday's Nasdaq Composite fell 0.91% while S&P 500 fell approximately 0.4% and Dow gained 0.1%. WSJ now reports SOX down 3.4% at the close, confirming substantial chip underperformance; AP reports AMD -8.8% and Broadcom -4.8%, while Nvidia closed $162.85 (-2.01%). Nasdaq still gained 2.3% for the week, so the decline is not a confirmed broad-market breakdown. There has been no new cash trading since Friday.
editorial.whatChanged: Since the 18:16 EST assessment, a WSJ closing report confirms SOX -3.4% rather than relying on an earlier intraday -3.7% estimate. AP confirms AMD -8.8%, Broadcom -4.8% and Brent settlement $95.84/bbl. These observations refine already known chip weakness and oil pricing, not a new directional catalyst. Open Watch still has 163 events and no newly verified feed update.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Confirmed SOX closing underperformance makes the tech-led risk-off pattern more credible, while Nasdaq's positive weekly return and slightly softer monthly PPI remain counterweights. Elevated 10Y and 2Y yields in the Friday WSJ report imply a +28.3bp curve using correct percentage-to-basis-point scaling, but the precise quote times are not synchronized. No fresh matched VXN/VIX, breadth or direct FedWatch reading validates an additional regime shift. Brent near $96 remains an inflation sensitivity, not evidence of a new overnight oil move.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 16 should test whether semiconductor selling continues or stabilizes after Friday's confirmed SOX loss. Tuesday November 17 brings expected retail-sales and earnings risk, particularly Nvidia's reported after-close release. Wednesday November 18 is the first session in which any Nvidia earnings surprise and guidance response could be observed. Base case remains bearish elevated downside with rebound potential if breadth and chips stabilize; neither a precise probability nor a future reaction can be claimed.
editorial.bullCase: A rebound that holds Friday lows, broadens Nasdaq participation and sees SOX outperform alongside lower volatility and easing yields would undermine the bearish skew. Weekly Nasdaq +2.3% and softer-than-consensus monthly PPI suggest potential demand, but a durable recovery has not been demonstrated. Positive Nvidia guidance is a conditional upside catalyst, not an observed outcome.
editorial.bearCase: Friday's SOX -3.4% close, AMD -8.8%, Broadcom -4.8% and Nvidia -2.01% show broad chip weakness. If Monday breaks Friday lows with negative breadth, rising volatility and persistent elevated yields, downside can extend into Tuesday. An unfavorable Nvidia release could amplify Wednesday losses, but its result and response remain unknown.
editorial.watchNext: Check Monday synchronized QQQ, SOX, VXN/VIX, breadth and matched Treasury yields, along with fresh Brent/WTI and direct CME FedWatch.
